findings.title: Reopening and saving a stdio MCP form loses structured argument boundaries
findings.trigger: The ordinary full stdio editor first saves a nonempty quoted argument containing spaces; the user reopens and saves without editing Args.
findings.expected: Keep the existing string[] argument boundaries.
findings.actual: args.join(" ") loses quoting, and submit unconditionally splitArgs parses the unquoted text into different array elements before the ordinary patch write.
findings.cause: The array-to-text initializer is not an inverse of the supported quoted-segment parser.
counterevidence: Plugin override locks args and is outside the finding.
The ordinary name/command validation and save guards do not preserve unchanged structured args.
Array copy/deepMerge preserves the newly changed array rather than restoring original boundaries.
Old MCP headers, TUI command split/join and plugin empty quoted-token cases have distinct producers and repair sites.
findings.validation: Ordinary source producer, UI entry, serialization/parser and patch data flow read statically; zero product/helper/language fixture/form/test/MCP/probe/settings/process/network execution. No runtime launch or connection result claimed.
findings.remediation: Use a lossless serializer compatible with the parser, a structured args editor, or preserve the original array when the field is unchanged.
findings.classificationNote: Single P3 static opinion shared by author, Root and independent reviewer; no duplicate item. Rename extra-fields remains an uncompleted boundary, not a candidate.
